record.paper_title: Doubly-Special Relativity: First Results and Key Open Problems
record.original_question: Which spacetime descriptions are compatible with the Doubly-Special Relativity framework? The robust results obtained so far concern only the energy-momentum sector, while the paper argues that introducing a second observer-independent scale may require a major revision of spacetime concepts, possibly even abandoning the absolute statement that two particles follow the same trajectory for all observers. The open problem is to identify a spacetime picture, possibly involving noncommutative geometry or only an approximate notion of spacetime, that is consistent with DSR kinematics and with the relation v = dE/dp if that relation is retained.

evidence.quote: 7.3. Which spacetimes are compatible with the DSR framework?
All robust results obtained so far in the DSR framework concern the energy-momentum sector. It is unclear which type of spacetime picture is required by the DSR framework.
What should we give up for the second observer-independent scale?

Perhaps this is taking us in the direction of considering spacetime as an approximate concept, only valid within a certain class of observations and with a certain level of approximation. Perhaps such a picture could be implemented through a description of spacetime in terms of noncommutative geometry.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Doubly-Special Relativity (DSR) is a framework that deforms the kinematics of Special Relativity by postulating, in addition to the invariant speed of light c, a second observer-independent scale (typically the Planck energy/length). The robust formulations of DSR developed so far specify a deformed Poincaré-type action on energy-momentum space, leading to modified dispersion relations and modified composition laws for momenta, while leaving the corresponding spacetime picture undetermined.

Problem: Identify a spacetime description compatible with the DSR framework. Specifically, construct (or prove the existence/uniqueness of) a notion of "spacetime" — possibly realized through a noncommutative geometry, or only as an approximate concept valid within a limited class of observations — that satisfies all of the following:

(a) It is invariant, in an appropriate operational sense, under the DSR-deformed relativistic transformations acting in the momentum sector, with two observer-independent scales c and an energy/length scale at the Planck regime.

(b) It is consistent with the deformed dispersion relations and deformed momentum composition laws characterizing DSR kinematics.

(c) Either (i) it preserves the absolute (observer-independent) statement that two pointlike particles emitted with the same energy-momentum follow the same worldline for all inertial observers, or (ii) it provides a precise alternative replacing that statement, specifying the operational meaning of "trajectory" and "coincidence of events" in the proposed framework.

(d) If the velocity relation v = dE/dp is retained as the group velocity of a wave packet, the proposed spacetime structure must reproduce this relation in the appropriate classical/low-energy limit.

Determine whether such a spacetime picture exists and, if so, characterize it.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem of identifying a spacetime picture compatible with DSR kinematics remains an active open issue. Candidate proposals involve κ-Minkowski and Snyder-type noncommutative geometries, but no consensus formulation has been established; later reviews continue to list this among key open problems in DSR, and recent work (e.g., 2025–2026 on CPT and Magueijo–Smolin noncommutative models) still grapples with consistency of discrete symmetries and the spacetime sector.

status_evidence.title: Doubly-Special Relativity: Facts, Myths and Some Key Open Issues
status_evidence.snippet: Discussion of remaining open issues in DSR, including which spacetime structures are compatible with the framework.
status_evidence.claim: A later review continues to flag the DSR spacetime question as an open issue.

status_evidence.title: CPT breaking in noncommutative Magueijo-Smolin model
status_evidence.snippet: Studies a specific noncommutative realization of a DSR model and finds problems with discrete symmetries.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work shows that consistent noncommutative spacetime realizations of DSR still face unresolved structural issues.

status_evidence.title: Dirac spinors for DSR and κ-Minkowski noncommutative spacetime
status_evidence.snippet: Connects DSR with κ-Minkowski noncommutative spacetime as a candidate compatible spacetime.
status_evidence.claim: κ-Minkowski is a leading but not definitive candidate for the DSR-compatible spacetime.
